subject: SIG questionnaire — exception request for cross-border key access
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@finbank.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: FinBank Procurement <procurement@finbank.com>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: SIG questionnaire + exception request for key access

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking the SIG. Attached is FinBank's completed SIG spreadsheet — we've flagged two control items where our security policy requires that customer encryption keys not be exported or accessed from outside the EU.

We're evaluating Redwood for a pilot (FIN-8421) and need confirmation of whether you can commit to either:
- Hosting customer-managed keys in an EU region with no US access, or
- A contractual, audited exception that allows Redwood engineering to perform occasional key operations from the US under strict controls (audit log, jumpbox, documented runbook).

We understand the latter is non-standard; the procurement and security teams asked us to surface the request early so we can evaluate timelines and any executive approvals needed. Can you confirm feasibility and, if an exception is required, what governance/contract language your side would need?

Attaching: FinBank_SIG.xlsx (completed), network_diagram.pdf

Olivia Grant
Senior Information Security Manager
FinBank

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@finbank.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire + exception request for key access

Hi Olivia — thanks for the SIG and the clear note.

Short answer: we treat key locality and customer-managed keys as high priority for Private deployments, but our hosted offering defaults to a US HSM region today. We need to review the exact control questions you flagged and propose options.

Next steps from our side:
- Internal compliance review (cc'd: Laura, Mina) to confirm whether a one-off, governed exception is allowable under our policy;
- Product/engineering feasibility check for an EU-only KMS path or a documented runbook for emergency key operations;
- If an exception is required, we'll escalate to leadership for an exec sign-off and proposed contract language.

Laura/Mina — can you review the attached SIG (FinBank_SIG.xlsx) and highlight any mandatory no-export controls we cannot reasonably accept? Also indicate what contractual mitigations (audit cadence, indemnity caps, time-limited exception) we should require.

Olivia — I'll follow up once we have internal guidance. If helpful, we can schedule a short call this week to walk through mitigations.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: mina_haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire + exception request for key access — technical feasibility

Karthik / Laura — quick technical note after looking at the network_diagram and the control flags in the SIG. Summary:

- EU-local KMS: We don't currently offer a fully EU-hosted KMS for the hosted product; Private (VPC) deployments support customer-managed HSMs in-region. Shipping an EU-only KMS in hosted would be a Q3 roadmap item (approx 10–12wk dev + 4–6wk validation) if prioritized.

- Short-term mitigations we can offer immediately:
  - Key wrap: customers provide key-encrypting key (KEK) stored in their HSM; Redwood stores only wrapped keys. That reduces risk but may not satisfy "no US access" controls.
  - Strict operational process: emergency unwrapping requires a documented ticket, two-person approval (security + engineering lead), live audit recording, and we can provide the full transcript to the customer.
  - Enhanced logging: immutable audit trail pushed to customer's S3/GCS bucket and retention locked for contractual period.

- Impact on timeline/regression: offering an emergency unwrapping process introduces operational burden and requires legal constraints (liability, scope, time-boxed).

If we need to sign a contractual exception, we should make it: time-bound (6–12 months), scoped (only named environment and accounts), and revocable. For the roadmap ask, we can provide a prioritized plan but we should not commit to product delivery dates without exec approval.

Happy to jump on a quick call with FinBank if they want to review the technical mitigations.

—Dev
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Requesting exec approval: FinBank SIG — exception & limited contractual commitment

Aditya — quick summary and ask:

- FinBank (potential mid-enterprise pilot, deal FIN-8421) has marked two SIG controls requiring keys to never be exported or accessed outside the EU. They will not proceed without either EU KMS hosting (hosted product) or a documented, auditable exception.
- Product says EU KMS for hosted is Q3; mitigations (key wrap + auditable emergency unwrapping + immutable logs) are feasible immediately but do not strictly satisfy "no US access" wording.
- Legal recommends we can offer a one-year, revocable exception with the following constraints:
  1) Emergency unwrapping only under defined incident classifications and with two-person approval (security + on-call eng lead).
  2) Quarterly third-party audit of the process (customer may receive redacted evidence).
  3) Indemnity/limitation language tightened for this exception.
  4) A contract credit ($20k) to account for operational overhead.

Ask: Can you sign off on providing a time-boxed exception with the constraints above and authorize Product to publish a non-binding roadmap note saying an EU-hosted KMS is on the Q3 roadmap (no firm date commitment)? We need an exec-level approval to proceed and to include this in the commercial terms.

If you approve, I'll draft the exception letter and the contract clause for Procurement/FinBank and coordinate with Karthik to close.

Laura Bennett
Head of Trust & Compliance, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Requesting exec approval: FinBank SIG — exception & limited contractual commitment

Laura / team — I approve the approach with the following conditions:

1) Exception is strictly time-limited to 12 months from contract execution.
2) Customer signs the exception letter and acknowledges the emergency unwrapping runbook and audit schedule.
3) Procurement agrees to the $20k operational credit and an SLA addendum limiting Redwood's exposure tied to the exception.
4) Product may state the EU-hosted KMS is on the Q3 roadmap but cannot provide dates or commit to SLAs until the feature exits beta.

Karthik — please confirm that Procurement at FinBank is comfortable with the credit and that they will accept the audit constraints. If yes, draft the exception letter and loop in Procurement for signature. Mina — please prepare the audit checklist and the redaction policy for customer evidence.

Aditya Rao
CEO (copying in-line authority for speed)

Olivia — thanks again for the patience. Quick update and proposed next steps: 

1) Internal decision: Redwood can provide a time-limited (12 month), revocable exception for emergency unwrapping under strict governance. Exec approval granted subject to contract language and procurement acceptance.

2) Commercial ask: we are prepared to apply a one-time $20k operational credit for overhead related to this arrangement; please confirm procurement is OK with this.

3) Technical mitigations: we'll implement key-wrap + immutable audit trail to your S3 (or equivalent) and run the two-person approval process documented in the runbook. Mina will produce the audit checklist; Dev will join the technical call.

4) Roadmap note: Product has agreed to list EU-hosted KMS as a Q3 roadmap item (no firm date).

Next actions for FinBank: confirm procurement acceptance of credit and sign the exception letter. I'll circulate the draft exception letter and the scope of the emergency unwrapping runbook by end of day. Can we schedule a 30-min call Thu to finalize?

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
